title: Expeditions change a persistent world
summary: Expedition outcomes can permanently affect the Outpost and the campaign record.
details: The Outpost, Archive, Job Board, and reports represent the current known state of a world shared by different crews. Records should be updated when new information or consequences are established.

title: Exploration comes before a fixed plot
summary: The campaign presents places, situations, mysteries, hazards, factions, and opportunities rather than a predetermined sequence of events.
details: Player decisions determine which leads receive attention and how discoveries change the shared world. The site records opportunities and known situations without assuming what the crew will do next.

title: Knowledge is progress
summary: Discoveries and verified information are rewards in their own right.
details: Field reports, maps, observations, artifact research, and environmental findings can expand what Expeditioners know. Only information discovered and established in play belongs in the public record.

title: Outpost projects change the settlement when completed
summary: Projects advance on progress tracks; filling a track completes the project.
details: A completed project records its result on the Outpost Sheet. Depending on the project, that result may create a facility, improve a capability, or add or remove a condition.

title: Outpost stress and consequences
summary: When all Outpost stress boxes are marked, a consequence absorbs further stress.
details: A consequence's severity determines how much stress it can absorb: Low absorbs 2, Moderate 4, High 6, and Critical 8. Current marked stress and active consequences are recorded on the Outpost Sheet.

title: Players choose expedition priorities
summary: Players decide which Gates, mysteries, threats, and Outpost projects to pursue.
details: Nowhere Expeditions uses a West Marches structure. Available opportunities are presented for the players to choose from; no expedition is mandatory and there is no fixed route through the campaign.

title: The Outpost is a shared campaign character
summary: The Outpost has capabilities, aspects, stress, consequences, facilities, projects, and conditions that matter to play.
details: Capabilities such as Industry, Research, Commerce, Security, Medicine, and Infrastructure describe what the settlement can do in the fiction. They are public-facing tools, not a substitute for other campaign procedures.

title: Unknown information stays marked as unknown
summary: Unverified details and unexplored mysteries are not filled in with guesses.
details: Use clear markers such as UNKNOWN, UNCLASSIFIED, NO DATA, or NOT YET SURVEYED when the campaign record does not establish an answer. Secret GM information is not published on player-facing pages.
